profile:
Name: Aditya Raj. Online handle: xreep. Pronoun: he.
Headline: Full-Stack Developer (JavaScript, Node.js, React). Intern at Unified Mentor. BCA student at Sarala Birla University (SBU), Ranchi.
Location: Dhanbad–Ranchi area, Jharkhand, India.

Looking for: internships and entry-level full-stack developer roles. Open to on-site or hybrid work in Ranchi.

Experience:
- Full-Stack Web Development Intern, Unified Mentor Private Limited (Internship, remote; company in Gurugram, Haryana). May 2026 to present. Built responsive web and mobile interfaces with React and React Native; integrated third-party REST APIs (weather, air quality) for live data features; implemented client-side logic for risk scoring, alerts and data visualization; designed privacy-focused features (on-device processing, user consent controls); used Git and GitHub for version control and code reviews.
- Graphics Design Lead, E-Cell, SBU (Institution's Innovation Council), part-time, on-site in Ranchi. September 2026 to present. Leads visual communication, promotional creatives and branding for the E-Cell ("From Ideas to Impact"). Designed the E-Cell logo concepts, brand kit and the Grand Opening event poster for the 18 September 2026 inauguration.
- GDG Group Member, Google Developer Group on Campus – SBU, part-time, on-site in Ranchi. October 2026 to present.

Education: Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA), Sarala Birla University, Ranchi. September 2024 to present. Grade: 7.5 CGPA.

Project — Raksha (github.com/xreep/raksha): an offline health guardian Android app for heat waves, floods and smog. It reads vitals on the phone, weighs them against local weather and air quality, and warns before it becomes an emergency. No account, no server, no vitals leave the device.
- Built for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement 26181 from Qualcomm (hardware category), with team 404hunt_06.
- On-device rule engine with six categories: heat stress (NOAA heat index), respiratory, cardiovascular, falls, dehydration, fatigue. Each gives a level, a plain-language recommendation and a 0-100 score.
- Live temperature, humidity and air quality, cached for offline use. Heat-index bands, AQI advisory, static flood and cyclone preparedness guidance.
- Emergency SOS: 30-second cancel window, then vitals and a location link are sent through a Cloudflare Worker relay to Telegram; with no data it opens a pre-filled SMS.
- Seven days of local history with trends. Privacy by design: no account, no server, no analytics.
- Stack: Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86, React 19, TypeScript, Expo Router, react-native-health-connect, expo-sqlite, Cloudflare Workers, Jest and Vitest. 1,457 tests across 63 suites in CI.
- Status: research prototype, not a medical device. Validated on one Android 15 device: Health Connect ingestion (heart rate, SpO2), rule engine on live data, AQI advisory, notifications, SMS fallback, Telegram relay. Roadmap: background sensing, Raksha Band firmware and BLE, encrypted storage, caregiver role, seven-day baselines, Hindi interface.
- Raksha Band: a planned wrist wearable (not built yet; firmware not written). Designed around a XIAO ESP32-C3 with MAX30101 heart rate, MAX30205 skin temperature, MPU6050 motion and fall detection, SHT40 air temperature and humidity, a LiPo battery and a buzzer. Pod about 40 x 32 x 14 mm. There is an interactive 3D concept model on the Projects page.

Skills: networking fundamentals (Cisco CCNA coursework), data analytics, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, Bootstrap, React.js, React Native, Expo, Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, REST APIs, Python, Java, Git, GitHub, version control, graphic design, team leadership, leadership, communication, community outreach, problem solving, strategy. Uses AI coding tools such as Claude.

DSA: practises data structures and algorithms on LeetCode (profile: leetcode.com/u/xreep) and takes part in LeetCode contests, mostly in Java.

Licenses and certifications:
- Oracle Cloud Infrastructure 2025 Certified AI Foundations Associate (Oracle, August 2025, credential ID 322001347OCI25AICFA). This is his exam-based certification.
- Cisco Networking Academy course completions through Sarala Birla University (2026): CCNA: Introduction to Networks (April 2026); CCNA: Enterprise Networking, Security, and Automation (June 2026); Python Essentials 1 and Python Essentials 2 (June 2026, with OpenEDG Python Institute); Introduction to Modern AI; Apply AI: Analyze Customer Reviews; Data Analytics Essentials; Introduction to Data Science (all June 2026). These are course completions, not the CCNA certification exam.
- Getting Started with Generative AI (IBM SkillsBuild); IIRS Outreach Programme – Merit Certificate (Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, ISRO); HTML and CSS Certifications (Dilwado.com).
All certificates with a file can be viewed in the Certifications section of the About page.
Site extras: the portfolio has a Playground (footer link) with ten small games he built in plain JavaScript: Stack Snake, Bug Hunt, Whack-a-Bug, Firewall (brick breaker), Deploy Dash, Stack Memory, Code Typing, Commit 2048, Bug Sweeper and Stackle (a tech word puzzle).
Events: attended the Blockchain and Web3 workshop by Kalp Studio at SBU.

Contact: email aditya8251358@gmail.com. His phone number is on his résumé. LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/adityaraj777. GitHub: github.com/xreep. LeetCode: leetcode.com/u/xreep.
Résumé: a one-page PDF résumé can be downloaded with the 'Résumé' button in the hero section or on the About page.
API Lab: the portfolio has a live public endpoint, GET /api/heat-index?tempC=..&humidity=..&aqi=.., that runs Raksha's real NOAA heat-index engine (ported from src/risk/heat-index.ts) and returns JSON. Try it on the API Lab page.
Changelog: the site has a changelog page listing every release of the portfolio itself.
